verifiedTopics: Second Amendment and drug-related armed violence
Limits on detention for noncriminal release violations

cases.role: Author of unanimous judgment and opinion
cases.panel: Barberis authored; Vaughan and Sholar concurred in judgment and opinion.
cases.holding: Affirmed the armed-violence conviction and rejected both facial and as-applied Second Amendment challenges to a law covering possession of cocaine while carrying an operational firearm.
cases.reasoning: The opinion concluded that a person simultaneously committing a felony and carrying an operational gun was outside the Amendment's protected class. Alternatively, it found historical support for the restriction, including analogies to disarming felons and temporary restrictions involving intoxicants.
cases.disposition: Affirmed the Jefferson County judgment, including the 18-year sentence.
cases.decisionScope: Constitutional merits of this statutory challenge. Not an assault-weapons-ban case, a general license requirement, or a ruling on every firearm possession by a nonviolent offender.
cases.publicationStatus: Final in official opinion index as retrieved November 1, 2026
cases.subsequentHistory: Illinois Supreme Court denied leave to appeal on January 28, 2026, Supreme Court docket 132483 (identifying appellate docket 5-23-0656). This is a denial of discretionary review, not a merits affirmance. Any later federal review was not verified.
cases.subsequentPinpoint: January 28, 2026 leave-to-appeal disposition list, PDF page 14, docket 132483
cases.primaryRead: All 10 pages of the official final report read; cover visually checked

policyComparison.status: Not comparable to the selected national party/Trump baselines
policyComparison.reason: The issue was concurrent cocaine possession and an operational gun. A platform's general Second Amendment position or Trump's DOJ position on common-use rifle bans does not resolve this narrower restriction.

laterLegalContext.court: Supreme Court of the United States
laterLegalContext.pinpoints: Majority slip opinion pages 3, 5-7, 15-16 n.6, 18-19 (PDF pages 7, 9-11, 19-20, 22-23)
laterLegalContext.holding: Held this federal section 922(g)(3) prosecution, based solely on regular marijuana use without individualized dangerousness, inconsistent with the Second Amendment; the government had not carried its historical-analogy burden.
laterLegalContext.smithComparison: Hemani expressly says its charge did not involve cocaine possession or drug trafficking. Smith concerned simultaneous cocaine possession and an operational firearm under Illinois armed-violence law. Hemani did not decide that Illinois statutory question.
laterLegalContext.reservedQuestions: The majority expressly reserved convicted-felon disarmament, addicts, presently intoxicated people, particular-drug risk laws and prosecutions supported by individualized danger evidence. Footnote 6 says the opinion should not cast doubt on specified felony and adjudicated-mental-disability restrictions that involve predeprivation process.
laterLegalContext.currentStatusLimit: No subsequent decision applying Hemani to Smith was verified. This is later legal context, not a reversal of Smith or a claim that its every rationale remains controlling.
laterLegalContext.governmentVsCourt: The U.S. Supreme Court ruling is distinct from the federal administration position it rejected; it is not a Trump endorsement or a measure of Barberis personal beliefs.
laterLegalContext.primaryRead: All 19 pages of the majority opinion read. All 39 PDF pages were text-diffed against the revised official version; the sole substantive correction concerned an unrelated drug-product example on slip page 2.

cases.role: Author of unanimous judgment and opinion
cases.panel: Barberis authored; Moore and Boie concurred in judgment and opinion.
cases.holding: Reversed an order releasing a defendant and required a new hearing because aggravated battery by strangulation can qualify for detention under the statute's residual clause when the actual conduct threatens or inflicts great bodily harm.
cases.reasoning: The court declined another district's narrower construction and read the residual clause to focus on conduct. It distinguished a charge of strangulation from a charge expressly requiring actual great bodily harm; eligibility was conditional on the facts, not automatic for every strangulation charge.
cases.disposition: Release order reversed; remanded for further proceedings consistent with the opinion. The appellate court did not itself decide guilt or impose a prison sentence.
cases.decisionScope: Statutory eligibility ruling in an interlocutory detention appeal. It did not decide whether Illinois should use cash bail or whether the SAFE-T Act is constitutional.
cases.publicationStatus: Final in official opinion index as retrieved November 1, 2026
cases.subsequentHistory: No later disposition of this case independently verified; the result on remand is not established by this opinion.
cases.primaryRead: All 8 pages of the official final report read

cases.panel: Boie authored; Vaughan and Barberis concurred in judgment and opinion.
cases.topic: Limits on pretrial detention and release-condition violations
cases.holding: Reversed renewed detention and directed release, with possible modified conditions, because later noncriminal electronic-monitoring violations could not support a second detention petition under section 110-6.1(d)(2).
cases.reasoning: The court read the statute as reserving those violations for the sanctions process. A later detention petition cannot bypass the legislature's specific revocation requirements; newly discovered facts under that provision concern the original detention decision.
cases.disposition: Reversed and remanded with directions for release; immediate mandate. The State could pursue a proper revocation motion if statutory requirements were met.
cases.decisionScope: Statutory limits on a second detention petition. The court did not decide the defendant's alternative contention that he posed no unmitigable threat, nor the underlying criminal charges.
cases.publicationStatus: Final in official opinion index as retrieved November 1, 2026
cases.subsequentHistory: No later disposition in this same case independently verified. Stewart v. Rosenblum, 2025 IL 131365, paragraph 21, later reports a trial court applying Farris; that background citation is not an Illinois Supreme Court affirmance of Farris.
cases.primaryRead: All 13 pages of the official final report read

policyComparison.status: Not comparable to the selected national party/Trump baselines
policyComparison.reason: The statutory distinction between noncriminal violations and revocation grounds is different from a policy position on cash bail.

cases.role: Joined the majority judgment and opinion
cases.panel: Welch authored; Barberis concurred in judgment and opinion. Cates concurred in the result with different reasoning.
cases.holding: Joined the majority rejecting a First Amendment challenge to Illinois's restriction on photographing completed ballots and affirming dismissal of the voter’s complaint.
cases.reasoning: The majority treated a government-issued ballot as a nonpublic forum, found the restriction viewpoint neutral, and identified ballot secrecy, protection from coercion and vote buying, and orderly voting as reasons for the restriction. Cates agreed only with dismissal on ripeness grounds and questioned a felony penalty for an innocent selfie; that separate view was not Barberis's opinion.
cases.decisionScope: Majority reached the constitutional merits despite dismissal posture. The case concerns completed-ballot photos, not voter identification, citizenship documentation, mail ballots, or election-fraud allegations.
cases.publicationStatus: Final in official opinion index as retrieved November 1, 2026
cases.subsequentHistory: U.S. Supreme Court denied certiorari October 4, 2021, docket 20-1731, styled Oettle v. Cadigan. A denial of discretionary review is not approval of the majority's reasoning. The Illinois denial of leave appears in the petition appendix but is not needed for the public summary.
cases.subsequentPinpoint: October 4 order list page 13 under CERTIORARI DENIED; 2021 term Journal printed page 20; petition Appendix 18 for Illinois leave denial March 24, 2021
cases.primaryRead: All 6 pages of the official final report read
